def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import glob
    import pandas as pd

    paths = sorted(glob.glob('data/legal/input/csn-data-book-2024-csv/CSVs/State MSA Identity Theft data/*.csv'))
    if not paths:
        raise FileNotFoundError('No files matched identity theft glob pattern')

    dfs = []
    for p in paths:
        # read as strings first to avoid dtype issues; convert later
        df = pd.read_csv(p, dtype=str)
        df['__source_file'] = p.split('/')[-1]
        dfs.append(df)

    out = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)
    return out

def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd
    import glob, os

    pattern = "data/legal/input/csn-data-book-2024-csv/CSVs/State MSA Fraud and Other data/*.csv"
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(pattern))
    if len(paths) == 0:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No files matched pattern: {pattern}")

    dfs = []
    for p in paths:
        df = pd.read_csv(p, dtype=str)
        df["__source_file"] = os.path.basename(p)
        dfs.append(df)

    out = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)
    return out

def process(loadIdentityTheft) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = loadIdentityTheft.copy()

    # Standardize expected columns (first = metro name, second = report count)
    metro_col = df.columns[0]
    count_col = df.columns[1]

    out = df[[metro_col, count_col, "__source_file"]].rename(
        columns={metro_col: "metropolitan_area", count_col: "identity_theft_reports"}
    )

    # Drop header/footnote/blank rows
    out["metropolitan_area"] = out["metropolitan_area"].astype(str)
    out = out[~out["metropolitan_area"].str.strip().isin([
        "nan",
        "Metropolitan Area",
        "Source: Consumer Sentinel Network Data Book 2024, Federal Trade Commission",
    ])]
    out = out[out["metropolitan_area"].str.strip() != ""]

    out["identity_theft_reports"] = pd.to_numeric(out["identity_theft_reports"], errors="coerce")
    out = out.dropna(subset=["identity_theft_reports"])

    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

def process(loadFraud) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = loadFraud.copy()

    # Heuristically pick metro and count columns (some files may have extra cols)
    cols = list(df.columns)
    metro_col = cols[0]

    # Prefer a column that looks like a report count
    candidate_cols = [c for c in cols if c != metro_col and c != "__source_file"]
    if len(candidate_cols) == 0:
        raise ValueError("No candidate count column found in fraud files")

    # Choose the first candidate as count column
    count_col = candidate_cols[0]

    out = df[[metro_col, count_col, "__source_file"]].rename(
        columns={metro_col: "metropolitan_area", count_col: "fraud_reports"}
    )

    out["metropolitan_area"] = out["metropolitan_area"].astype(str)
    out = out[~out["metropolitan_area"].str.strip().isin([
        "nan",
        "Metropolitan Area",
        "Source: Consumer Sentinel Network Data Book 2024, Federal Trade Commission",
    ])]
    out = out[out["metropolitan_area"].str.strip() != ""]

    out["fraud_reports"] = pd.to_numeric(out["fraud_reports"], errors="coerce")
    out = out.dropna(subset=["fraud_reports"])

    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

def process(cleanIdentityTheft, cleanFraud) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    it = cleanIdentityTheft.copy()
    fr = cleanFraud.copy()

    # Aggregate within metro across states (same MSA can appear in multiple state files)
    itAgg = it.groupby("metropolitan_area", as_index=False)["identity_theft_reports"].sum()
    frAgg = fr.groupby("metropolitan_area", as_index=False)["fraud_reports"].sum()

    merged = itAgg.merge(frAgg, on="metropolitan_area", how="inner")
    merged["itExceedsFraud"] = merged["identity_theft_reports"] > merged["fraud_reports"]

    exists = bool(merged["itExceedsFraud"].any())
    return pd.DataFrame([{ "exists_identity_theft_exceeds_fraud": exists }])

operators.customDisplayName: Aggregate identity theft and fraud report counts by metropolitan_area (sum across all source files); inner-join on metropolitan_area; compute boolean identity_theft_reports > fraud_reports; output single-row flag exists_identity_theft_exceeds_fraud indicating whether any metro satisfies condition
